# Patina

> Patina is a deterministic-simulation runtime for Rust. It runs ordinary `std`
> programs (single Rust sources, whole Cargo packages, or WebAssembly modules)
> under a cooperative scheduler, a virtual clock, an in-memory filesystem, and a
> simulated network, so every run is a pure function of a seed. Runs are recorded
> to a trace and replayed byte-for-byte. Seed-driven fault injection (crashes,
> torn writes, network loss/jitter, sleep jitter) and a FoundationDB-style
> cooperative-SUT SDK (`buggify!`) turn a normal test into a deterministic
> distributed-systems fuzzer. Everything below is the `cargo patina` CLI surface
> and is verified against the current build.

Patina has no host fallback: a supported `std` call is deterministic or the run
fails closed (a missed interposer is a refusal, never a silent escape). A trace
carries its seed, fault config, and buggify config, so `replay` is flag-free.

## Targets (families)

The verb infers the target from the artifact's magic bytes: `\0asm` -> WASI
(`wasm32-wasip1`); Mach-O/ELF -> native (linked shim); a directory / `Cargo.toml`
with no `--target` -> the Cargo package family (in-process boundary API), except
`test <DIR|Cargo.toml>` which selects native libtest harness mode. A
`.rs`/dir/`Cargo.toml` source argument is built on the fly, then run.

## CLI verbs

- `cargo patina build <SOURCE.rs|DIR|Cargo.toml> [--output PATH] [--target native|wasi] [--release] [--yield-points]`
  Build a deterministic artifact. Default `--target native`. `--yield-points`
  instruments basic blocks (LLVM SanitizerCoverage) so atomics-only race windows
  become schedulable; native-only. Prints `PATINA_NATIVE_BUILD output=...` /
  `PATINA_WASI_BUILD output=...`.
- `cargo patina run <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--seed N | --record PATH] [--coverage-out PATH] [FAULT OPTIONS] [--buggify[=PERMILLE]] [-- ARGS]`
  Run under the deterministic runtime. `--seed` (default 0) drives everything.
  `--record PATH` writes a trace. Native yield-point binaries emit
  `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT`; `--coverage-out PATH` writes a `patina.covmap/v1`
  edge-counter map and refuses plain native binaries with a `build --yield-points` hint.
- `cargo patina test [--seed N | --record PATH] [FAULT OPTIONS] [CARGO OPTIONS]`
  The Cargo package family under Patina.
- `cargo patina test <DIR|Cargo.toml> --harness-target NAME --exact MOD::test [--seed N | --seeds N] [--release] [--yield-points] [FAULT/BUGGIFY/SCHEDULE/LIVENESS OPTIONS]`
  Native libtest harness mode: rebuilds the named Cargo test target shim-linked,
  stages it under `target/patina/dst/...`, runs the exact libtest filter with one
  libtest thread, and records the first failing seed with test/replay repros.
- `cargo patina replay <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> <TRACE> [--coverage-out PATH] [host inputs]`
  Reproduce a recording. Flag-free: seed, fault knobs, buggify, and guest argv
  are restored from the trace (the trace is authoritative; a re-supplied semantic
  flag that conflicts is refused). A fingerprint or operation mismatch fails
  closed with a nonzero exit.
- `cargo patina trace info <TRACE> [--timeline ID]` / `trace events <TRACE> [--kind LIST] [--task SEL]... [--seq A..B] [--first N|--last N] [--notable]` / `trace stats <TRACE>` / `trace diff <A> <B> [--context N]`
  Inspect an existing trace without executing a guest. `info` prints metadata,
  timelines, resolved event count, and virtual-time span. `events` prints the
  shared decoded event view; `--kind` accepts operation tags or categories
  (`filesystem`, `network`, `scheduling`, `sleep`, `clock`, `entropy`, `crash`,
  `other`), and `--task` accepts a task id or `main`. `stats` aggregates totals,
  per-kind/category/task counts, notable events, and a virtual-time histogram.
  `diff` compares two traces, exits 0 when identical and 1 when metadata/events
  diverge, and reports the first operation/outcome/length divergence.
- `cargo patina audit <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--allow SYMBOL]...`
  Strict fail-closed import allowlist. Any un-interposed effect symbol is a
  finding. Audit source-first (or a `cargo patina build` artifact): only a
  shim-linked binary shows the true post-interposition residual, so a stock
  prebuilt binary is refused unless `--raw`.
- `cargo patina explore run <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--seeds N] [--seed-start N] [RUN OPTIONS]`
  Sweep seeds, building once and running that artifact per seed. Stops at the
  first failing seed with `PATINA_EXPLORE_FAILURE seed=S exit=E repro="cargo patina run ... --seed S"`;
  the JSON envelope's `message` carries the same repro. Otherwise
  `PATINA_EXPLORE_COMPLETE start=... seeds=...`.
- `cargo patina campaign <ARTIFACT|SOURCE> [--gens N] [--out-dir DIR] [--seed-start N] [--plateau-after N] [--allow-unmet-sometimes[=MIN_GENS]] [--buggify] [--swarm] [--sched-pct] [--faults]`
  Config-driven deterministic fault-and-schedule sweep: every generation's seed
  and knobs are a pure function of the generation number, outcomes are
  classified into eight classes, novel failure signatures are deduped with saved
  traces, SDK site coverage is folded into `<out-dir>/sites.json` (schema
  `patina.campaign.sites/v1`), and native yield-point edge coverage is folded
  into `<out-dir>/coverage/` (schema `patina.coverage.campaign/v1`) with a
  plateau report controlled by `--plateau-after`. Registered `sometimes!` sites
  that are never satisfied fail the campaign by default unless explicitly waived.
- `cargo patina coverage <BINARY> <MAP|CAMPAIGN-OUT-DIR> [--focus CRATE::module] [--top N]`
  Read-only offline symbolization for native yield-point coverage. Resolves
  covmap PCs from the `patina_yield_point` anchor, demangles symbols, rolls edges
  up by crate/module/function, refuses campaign stores whose recorded artifact
  hash does not match `<BINARY>`, and emits human tables or a
  `patina.coverage/v1` JSON envelope.
- `cargo patina sites [--crate NAME] [--module PATH] [--group NAME] [--site LABEL] [--all] [--exercised FILE|OUTDIR] [--kind KIND] [--runtime driven|observed|invisible] [--no-cache]` / `sites --selftest`
  Static inventory of Patina SDK assertion/oracle sites, Rust assert/debug_assert,
  proptest/quickcheck, and antithesis-sdk assertions in the current workspace.
  JSON output is schema `patina.sites/v1`; per-file cache is
  `.patina/out/sites-cache.json` unless `--no-cache` is set. `--exercised FILE`
  reads raw `PATINA_SDK_REPORT` line(s); `--exercised OUTDIR` reads a campaign's
  `OUTDIR/sites.json`. Both join runtime counters by label or dynamic-label
  file:line.
- `cargo patina minimize <TRACE> --output PATH -- <ORACLE>` / `minimize --scenario --seed N -- <ORACLE>`
  Delta-debug a failing trace, or shrink the seed/params that trigger a failure.

## Fault + buggify knobs (seed-driven, default off; recorded into the trace)

- `--fs-crash-at open|write|sync|close[:N]`, `--fs-torn-granularity block|byte`, `--fs-error-permille N`, `--fs-short-permille N`
- `--sleep-jitter-nanos MIN..MAX`, `--net-jitter-nanos MIN..MAX`, `--net-drop-permille N`, `--net-latency-nanos N`
- `--buggify[=PERMILLE]`, `--buggify-activation-permille N`, `--buggify-cutoff-nanos N`, `--buggify-after-setup`

## Output options (all verbs; stripped before routing, never reach the guest)

- `--format human|json` (default human). `json` usually prints ONE result
  envelope on stdout (schema `patina.result/v1`) and folds captured guest output
  into it; `coverage --format json` emits `patina.coverage/v1`, and `trace
  events --format json` is the streaming exception and emits
  `patina.trace.events/v1` JSON Lines. Human output is unchanged by default.
  NOTE: the selector is `--format`, not
  `--output`, because `--output PATH` is already the build/minimize artifact path.
- `--render OUT.html` (run/replay with a trace): write a self-contained,
  single-file HTML timeline — per-task lanes over trace sequence, colored by
  category (scheduling, sleep, network, filesystem, crash, entropy, clock), a
  metadata panel rendered generically from the trace JSON, per-task rollups, and
  a notable-events list (crashes, boundary errors, dropped datagrams). No
  external assets. Large traces aggregate into density buckets with a visible
  banner. Rendering only reads the trace, so it never changes a replay hash.
- `--report OUT.html`: like `--render` but only on failure; the page leads with a
  failure summary (what fired, exit code, the result/violation lines).
- `--no-config`: ignore `.patina/config.toml` for this invocation. `PATINA_*` env
  defaults still apply unless the caller scrubs them.

## Repository config (`.patina/config.toml`)

- Discovered by walking up from cwd; first `.patina/config.toml` wins.
- `[groups.NAME] paths=["glob"] labels=["glob"]` tags `cargo patina sites`
  rows; generated cache files live under `.patina/out/`, and Patina creates
  `.patina/.gitignore` with `/out/` on first write.
- `[defaults.VERB] key = value` supplies verb defaults. Keys are registry-backed
  long flag names without `--` (campaign uses `generations` for `--gens`).
  Value grammar is the same registry `Kind` grammar as the parser.
- Precedence: explicit flag > `PATINA_<KEY>` env default > config file > built-in
  default. Config-file defaults emit `PATINA_CONFIG applied=<verb>:<keys>
  path=<file>` and JSON `config.applied[]` provenance. Replay refuses
  `[defaults.replay]`; campaign child `run` processes get `--no-config` and have
  run-default env names scrubbed.

### JSON result envelope (`patina.result/v1`)

One line of JSON on stdout. Always: `schema`, `verb`, `result`
(`ok|violation|failure|error`), `exit_code`. When applicable: `family`
(`native|wasi|cargo`), `artifact`, `fingerprint`, `seed`, `render`, `findings`
(audit import/finding strings), `finding_details` (structured audit symbol,
category, provenance), `output_path` + `content_hash` (build), `markers` (extracted
`PATINA_*`/`*_VIOLATION`/`BUG_CAUGHT` lines), `result_line`, `stdout`, `stderr`,
`message`, optional `config` provenance, optional native `coverage` =
`{edges_total, edges_covered, covered_permille, hits_total, hits_max, saturated,
map_path?}`, and `trace` =
`{path, format_version, timelines[], event_count, metadata}` where `metadata` is
the raw trace metadata (seed, faults, buggify, guest_argv, and any future fields,
rendered generically). `trace info --format
json` is a normal `patina.result/v1` envelope with a nested
`patina.trace.info/v1` `trace_info` payload; `trace stats --format json` and
`trace diff --format json` likewise nest `patina.trace.stats/v1` and
`patina.trace.diff/v1` payloads. `trace events --format json` emits
`patina.trace.events/v1` JSONL (header/events/summary; event lines carry raw
`operation`/`outcome`).

## SDK macros (crate `patina-dst`, default features = dependency-light SDK)

Instrument a system-under-test; every default-feature macro is a no-op under a
plain `cargo build` (adopters pay nothing) and lowers to the runtime only under
Patina. The default-off `macros` feature re-exports `#[patina_dst::test]` for
dev-dependency use under plain `cargo test`.

- `#[patina_dst::test]`: point-solution DST test. The plain test process finds
  `cargo-patina` via absolute `PATINA_CLI` or `cargo-patina` on `PATH`, rebuilds
  the same libtest target shim-linked, sweeps 20 seeds by default (or macro args
  such as `seed = 7`, `seeds = 200`, `buggify`, `fs_crash_at = "write:3"`), and
  panics with the failing seed plus `cargo patina test` / `cargo patina replay`
  repro commands. Missing CLI discovery is a failure, never a skip.
- `patina_dst::buggify!("label")` -> bool: fires on a rare, seed-deterministic path.
- `patina_dst::buggify_with_prob!("label", 0.9)`, `patina_dst::buggify_delay!("label")`,
  `patina_dst::buggify_knob!("label", default, lo, hi)` -> value.
- `patina_dst::always!(cond, "label")`: fatal invariant; a violation emits
  `PATINA_ALWAYS_VIOLATION` and aborts.
- `patina_dst::sometimes!(cond, "label")`, `patina_dst::reachable!("label")`: coverage.
- `patina_dst::lifecycle::setup_complete()`, `patina_dst::lifecycle::event!("name")`.
- `patina_dst::rng()`: seed-bridged deterministic entropy. `patina_dst::is_simulated()`.
- Explicit-context API (crate `patina-dst-runtime`): `patina_dst_runtime::run` /
  `run_with`, `Context`, `RuntimeBuilder`. Deterministic async lives in
  `patina-dst-async` (`block_on`, `spawn`, TCP/UDP futures) over that `Context`.

## Interpreting results

- Exit 0 = clean. A nonzero exit is the guest's own code; a violation
  (`*_VIOLATION`, `BUG_CAUGHT`, an `always!` abort, or a replay mismatch)
  classifies as `violation` under `--format json`. A CLI-side error (bad flags,
  build failure, refused replay) exits 2.
- `PATINA_SCHEDULE_REPORT` (stderr) reports per-task scheduling boundaries and
  warns (`vacuous_threads>0`) when a spawned thread ran zero interposed ops — i.e.
  its interleavings were not actually explored (use `build --yield-points`).
- `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT` (stderr) reports native yield-point edge coverage
  (`edges_covered/edges_total`, hit totals/max, saturation); suppress with
  `PATINA_COVERAGE_REPORT=0`.
- `PATINA_SDK_REPORT` (stderr) reports buggify site registration/activation/firing; each `site=` row ends with `|@<file:line>`.
- A trace is compact JSON: inspect it with `jq . run.patina`.

## Docs

- `TUTORIAL.md`: instrument a program with `buggify!`, sweep seeds, catch a
  planted bug, replay it, and render the timeline.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `VALIDATION.md`: design, slice status,
  and the verification gates.
- `testbeds/`: real end-to-end guests — `workq` (the flagship durable-work-queue
  demo), `pubsub` (a tokio broker on the interposed reactors), and more; see
  `testbeds/README.md` and each testbed's `run-patina.sh`.
